newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's daughter could be "common sense" adviser.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's daughter could be "common sense" adviser.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's younger daughter, Tatyana Dyachenko, could be appointed to a formal political role in the Kremlin, most probably as a "common sense" adviser to the president, first deputy premier Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.

Chubais, who was head of the Kremlin administration until March and who ran Yeltsin's re-election campaign with Dyachenko last year, stressed in an interview with Kommersant Daily newspaper that he had no inside knowledge of any appointment.
But asked to comment on speculation she would soon be given a formal role, Chubais said she was already, in reality, an adviser to her father and a "highly professional" one at that.

He said that if she were appointed, she would deal with political issues: "Not from the point of view of high politics and not from the point of view of the interests of some power lobby but from the point of view of common sense."
Chubais said common sense often got lost in the complex world of politics and Dyachenko had provided that insight during the election campaign.
"Tatyana Borisovna, in my view, was then and still is a representative of common sense in the high-level power structures," he concluded.
Aged 36, Dyachenko's role has often been compared to that of French President Jacques Chirac's daughter, Claude, who is an official presidential aide. The two women are said to have met.

Dyachenko, who has two children including a son called Boris Yeltsin, was credited with softening Yeltsin's image during the campaign, helping to persuade him to ditch hardline aides and sidestep criticism of the bloody intervention in Chechnya.
Chubais took the opportunity in the Kommersant Daily interview to deny rumours, which swirled in Moscow last year, that Dyachenko and he were romantically involved.

Listing a number of what he said were orchestrated smear campaigns against him, the married 41-year-old deputy premier told the paper: "There was a public discussion -- was Tatyana Dyachenko Chubais's lover? That campaign ended."
"All the allegations have been fully rejected," he said.
